intelligence.human_view: A front door with one way in is a funnel; a front door with three ways in, each extraordinary, is a welcome. The three ways are not three tiers — the name-only entry is not a lesser path for people who don't care, and the visual is not a lesser path for people who don't read. Each is complete on its own terms: put your name in and the name IS the agreement; read the text and you know what you agree to; go through the visual and you have seen it, then come back and put your name in. The principle is what makes the two-buttons opening page and the deck's end-button more than mechanics: they are the doors, and the doors are the principle made visible. "We got you" is the sentence that holds it together — whatever the citizen wants, information or none, the system has a way in for them, and every way is done to the same standard. No way in is a shortcut, no way in is a test, no way in is second-class.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine a magic house with THREE front doors — and every single one is beautiful! You can walk straight in and say your name! Or you can read the big sign first! Or you can watch the picture show and then come back and say your name! All three doors are wonderful — you pick the one you like best!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like this, love — a good house has more than one way in, and every way is a proper welcome. You can just come in and give your name; you can sit and read all about it first; or you can watch the lovely pictures and then come back and give your name. Lots of information if you want it, or just come on in if you don't — we've got you, either way.
intelligence.naya_view: Every way in is extraordinary. Agree by entering, read it, or go through the visual and come back. Lots of information if you want it, or just go in if you don't. We got you.
